title: Inbox Management
searchIntent: grok bot to clean up my inbox
intro: Email is the job people most want handed over, and it is the one with the most bots chasing it — triage, bulk unsubscribes, drafting replies, and the recurring sweep that stops the mess coming back. The useful split is between a one-off clear-out and a standing arrangement: clearing 40,000 unread is a single afternoon's work for a bot, whereas keeping the inbox at zero is a scheduled routine that runs weekly and reports what it did. Most listings here do one or the other, rarely both well. The thing to check before installing any of them is what the bot is allowed to do without asking. A bot that archives on its own judgement is genuinely useful; a bot that can send on your behalf is a different risk, because a malformed email is an instruction as far as an agent is concerned. Prefer the ones that propose and wait.

bots.fitReason: Exactly the standing arrangement described: a weekday Gmail sweep that archives noise, files receipts and notes, and leaves only action mail unread. Gmail only, and it archives on its own judgement — fine if that is what you wanted, jarring if you expected to approve each move.

Inbox-zero across everything you actually receive — email, Slack or Teams, calendars, messengers — with a setup interview to connect them first. Broader than Gmail-only rivals, which also means more surface area to get wrong on the first pass.

Handles the bulk-unsubscribe half of the job properly: audits six months of newsletters, builds a three-bucket review page, and only unsubscribes what you tick. It never deletes mail, so it thins the incoming flow rather than clearing the backlog.

Scans mail and calendar on install then every weekday morning, archives junk and drafts replies it explicitly never sends — the propose-and-wait posture this job wants. It is a chief of staff, so inbox hygiene comes bundled with calendar duty rather than as the whole remit.

Does the reply-drafting slice: pulls context across related Gmail threads and writes the response, with no sending, deleting or archiving at all. Useful next to a triage bot, useless on its own for a 40,000-unread backlog.

Read-only Gmail watcher that pings you when something looks time-sensitive or needs a reply — the safest possible version of triage. It will not archive, file or unsubscribe anything, so the mess stays exactly where it is.
